classification.difficultyReason: Derives the cosine double-angle identity by equating geometric expressions for the base of an isosceles triangle.

content.prompt: $ABC$ is an isosceles triangle, with $AB=AC=1$. Suppose $\angle BAC=2\theta$.

spec.description: Unfilled isosceles triangle with equal-side ticks, the whole apex angle marked 2 theta, and a red dashed apex-to-base-midpoint segment. No right-angle marker is added.
spec.mathematics: AB=AC=1 from the stem; the dashed segment bisects the apex angle and the base.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied figure only; no derived lengths are shown.

answer.worked:
Let $D$ be the midpoint of $BC$. In an isosceles triangle, $AD$ is perpendicular to $BC$ and bisects $\angle BAC$, so $\angle BAD=\theta$.
$$\begin{align*}\sin\theta&=\frac{BD}{1},\\BD&=\sin\theta,\\BC&=2BD\\BC&=2\sin\theta.\end{align*}$$

Equating the expressions for $BC^2$ from parts a and b gives
$$\begin{align*}2(1-\cos2\theta)&=(2\sin\theta)^2\\2(1-\cos2\theta)&=4\sin^2\theta,\\1-\cos2\theta&=2\sin^2\theta.\end{align*}$$
